summary.headline: Bodal Chemicals Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 884 crore (+77% YoY), EBITDA INR 128 crore at 14.4% margin, and net profit INR 81 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue rose 77% YoY to INR 884 crore, with EBITDA of INR 128 crore (14.4% margin) and net profit of INR 81 crore. H1 FY27 consolidated revenue reached a record INR 1,599 crore (+67%), with EBITDA of INR 203 crore (+114%) and net profit of INR 112 crore versus INR 16 crore in H1 FY26. Management credited higher H acid and vinyl sulphone prices, linked to structural changes in China, and volume growth in dye intermediates. The benzene downstream plant, which had lost about INR 30 crore EBITDA a year, is now ramping up, with utilisation above 85% in October. Management guided to a 12% margin on INR 3,000 crore+ FY27 revenue, but declined to give H acid or vinyl sulphone price data or capacity expansion plans.

segments.name: Dye intermediates
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 345 crore (+88% YoY); H1 consolidated INR 562 crore. H acid and vinyl sulphone are ~35% of this business, with about 40% captively consumed. Management says dye intermediate utilisation is at optimum and no capacity expansion is planned for now.

segments.name: Dyestuff
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 212 crore (+60% YoY); H1 consolidated INR 361 crore. Q2 volume was 5,314 MT versus 3,742 MT in Q1 FY26. Utilisation is about 65-70% on a multi-year average, and management expects realisations to improve in Q3 after a roughly 3-month lag.

segments.name: Basic chemicals
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 99 crore (+199% YoY); H1 consolidated INR 183 crore, driven by higher sulphur prices. About 50% of output is captively used in dye intermediates.

segments.name: Chlor-alkali
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 91 crore (+8% YoY); H1 consolidated INR 178 crore (+6%), helped by better realisations. Punjab site has spare land for expansion.

segments.name: Benzene downstream (Saykha)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR 108 crore (Q1 INR 65 crore; Q2 hit by a technical issue). October run-rate was above INR 300 crore, with utilisation around 85%, and management sees INR 350-400 crore annual potential. Management expects it to contribute to net profit from Q3.

segments.name: TCCA
segments.commentary: Roughly break-even at EBITDA. Output rose from about 100 to about 300 tonnes per month after anti-dumping duty. Management plans to double capacity in the next few months using domestically sourced equipment, after Chinese equipment could not be exported.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue of INR 3,000 crore+ is 'very much achievable' and management is targeting about 12% EBITDA margin for the year.
Q3 FY27 expected to show a further top-line and margin increase on the existing order book, and management expects Q4 to be similar to Q2 and Q3, with H2 expected to be better than H1.

Other income of about INR 15 crore expected in H2 from sale of Punjab and Ahmedabad land. Pending Punjab electricity duty subsidy of about INR 50 crore has accrued but is not booked, and about INR 5 crore Gujarat subsidy is yet to be received.
Sustainable tax rate of 25%. Management expects interest cost to fall gradually as term debt is repaid.
FY28: volume growth expected from benzene derivatives, TCCA and dyestuff utilisation. Management says a normalised case could still deliver about INR 2,800 crore revenue and 14-15% EBITDA margin.
capex_capacity: Benzene downstream plant utilisation was about 50% in H1 and above 85% in October, and management expects close to 100% by quarter-end.
Management says it will not expand H acid or dye intermediate capacity for now, and will revisit only if China's structural shift is confirmed, likely after Q4 FY27.
Any brownfield expansion could be commissioned in 1.5-2 years, and a capacity addition could be completed in under 12 months.
Organic and inorganic opportunities of INR 100-200 crore are being considered, with internal projects at Bharuch and the Punjab chlor-alkali site.
TCCA capacity is to be doubled within a few months using domestically procured equipment.
demand_pricing: H acid price peaked near INR 1,800/kg and corrected to about INR 1,600-1,650/kg, which management says is passing through to dyestuff. Management expects it to hold through January.
Vinyl sulphone is at about INR 440-450/kg, with management expecting it to hold for some time. Average realisations were about INR 320/kg in Q1 and INR 360-370/kg in Q2.
H acid average realisation was about INR 600/kg in Q1 and about INR 900/kg in Q2. Management said there is no assessment of the per-kg spread on external H acid sales.
Management says dyestuff prices lag intermediates by about 3 months, so Q3 realisations should improve over Q1 and Q2.
China export trends (H acid, vinyl sulphone, and benzene and dyestuff products) are cited as possible signs of structural change, with no significant new Chinese capacity in recent years.

Aniline is about INR 250/kg and sulphur about INR 90-100/kg, with sulphuric acid falling from about INR 110/kg to about INR 90/kg. Management says about 50% of sulphuric acid output is sold externally.
TCCA prices are about INR 150-160/kg after anti-dumping duty, against INR 110-120/kg before. Management says costs are about INR 160/kg and margins are thin.

qa_highlights.question: Will H acid prices and demand hold after the Chinese festive season, and is there buyer resistance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said orders are committed through January at about INR 1,600-1,650/kg, and it will reassess in December for February-March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables and cash flow from operations weaken in H1 despite higher profit?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed it to revenue up 70-80% and higher working capital. He said receivables will stabilise once turnover is steady for one or two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for cash deployment and debt repayment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most free cash will go to repaying term debt, with total debt flat versus March 2026 because working capital rose. It also said it may pursue acquisitions while keeping ratios strong.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no H acid capacity expansion despite strong demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is already the largest producer, will expand only if the structural shift is confirmed, and that a decision is likely after Q4 FY27. It noted an expansion could be done in under 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TCCA outlook after anti-dumping duty, and is there new competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TCCA is near break-even, with capacity rising from 100 to 300 tonnes per month and a plan to double capacity locally. It said new entrants face technical barriers because the plant uses Chinese technology, though some players are evaluating entry.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company's EBITDA margin compare with Kiri Industries, and why is the gap large?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dyestuff is a low-margin selling tool for intermediates, benzene derivatives ran at about 50% utilisation in Q2, and TCCA adds little margin. Management said Kiri's EBITDA margin was about 18% versus about 14.5% for the company.

risks_watch: Receivables and working capital are rising with turnover, which is holding back free cash flow and debt reduction.
Price sustainability: H acid, vinyl sulphone and benzene derivative prices depend on China's structural shift and buyer acceptance after China's festive season.
Crude and raw material costs (aniline, sulphur) are elevated, and management expects some top-line correction if crude normalises at $70-80.
Gross margin has been broadly flat at about 40% standalone, so the H acid price rise has not yet lifted gross margin.
Benzene downstream ramp-up and dyestuff realisation improvement in Q3 must come through, and the INR 50 crore Punjab subsidy must be booked.
TCCA capacity expansion and the planned domestic equipment sourcing must deliver margin improvement.
Management has not provided H acid or vinyl sulphone average realisation for Q2 on a precise basis, and the figures given were rough estimates.
summary.management_tone: Confident on near-term pricing and margins but conservative on long-term capacity, with management repeatedly declining to commit beyond the next quarter. Specific figures such as H acid and vinyl sulphone realisations were given only as approximate ranges, and some questions were deferred to IR.

key_quotes: It is very clear that receivable is going to pile up.
We are not looking for anything too big in size because of the pending debt on the book.
Our problem is that our utilization is very less, which we are fixing that problems.

So, anybody wanting to enter this space, it's not going to be easy technically, because our plant was set up by a team of Chinese people, and there is a lot of Chinese technology and equipment's involved in the entire plant.
We are the largest manufacturer with two plants, and we are also the largest manufacturer of another key dye intermediate called vinyl sulphone.

I think this could be structural shift, but I think it is a little bit too soon right now because it's only been a few months, and I think we want to really see how things are in the last quarter of the financial year and then maybe we can decide.

adds.what: TCCA capacity doubling using domestically sourced equipment (from ~300 t/month base)
Benzene downstream (Saykha) plant ramp-up to ~100% utilisation (already-built capacity, not new)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue of INR 3,000 crore+ and ~12% EBITDA margin, backed mainly by price gains (H acid, vinyl sulphone), H1 run-rate of INR 1,599 crore, the Saykha benzene plant ramping to ~85-100% utilisation and an existing order book, with no new dye-intermediate capacity planned.
